key_insight: CommCP integrates LLM-based inter-robot communication with conformal prediction to make multi-agent coordination both communicatively efficient and uncertainty-aware. This enables heterogeneous robots to ask/answer targeted questions and decide when to act or request more information based on calibrated confidence.
problem_solved: Reduces excessive or unreliable communication and unsafe decisions in cooperative multi-robot tasks where robots must interpret natural-language assignments, gather scene information, and allocate manipulation duties under uncertainty.
method: Use LLMs as a shared communication and reasoning channel for generating/answering task-relevant questions and proposing action plans among heterogeneous robots.
Apply conformal prediction to calibrate LLM outputs and agent decisions, producing confidence sets that guide when to act, ask for clarification, or defer tasks.
Optimize communication and task allocation by letting agents only exchange high-value messages (confidence-driven filtering) and using calibrated uncertainty to allocate skills to the right robot.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building scalable, safety-conscious multi-robot systems that leverage LLM reasoning while bounding risk via statistical calibration. AI/ML practitioners can reduce communication overhead and failure rates in real-world collaborative robotics and multi-agent applications.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: heterogeneous robots → LLM communication hub → conformal prediction module → coordinated actions (showing feedback loops)
Bar/line chart: communication rounds and task success rate (baseline vs. CommCP) to highlight efficiency gains
Confidence visualization: example message with calibrated confidence bands and decision thresholds (act / ask / defer)
Icon set: different robot types, natural-language task card, message bubbles, and a shield/legal-style icon for calibrated safety
paper_title: CommCP: Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination via LLM-Based Communication with Conformal Prediction
paper_authors: Xiaopan Zhang, Zejin Wang, Zhixu Li, Jianpeng Yao, Jiachen Li
